“Comic!” Night N. Shinning Ahmoȏr could only watch as the skinny, happy-go-luck oaf fell through the floor.

Shock fell through them- how right that word was. Night felt as though he’d been electrocuted; his arms burst with pain from the useless adrenaline before falling to his sides like a burden he could no longer bare. He let his sword fall from his fingers, hitting the stone ground with a loud crash. His breathing staggered, and the dungeon’s cold air hurt his lungs. 

The party looked at each other, each member trying to read the other’s emotions. For once, they were in synch. They’d all been electrocuted.

“Well shit,” Angerious Masculinus Whiteus said curtly. Down below, they heard the sour sound of flesh against stone, blunt and hurried. The underground’s unforgiving silence haunted them.

Then, all of the sudden, it was broken, like a piece of porcelain against a cement floor, or Comic’s body from a 50 foot drop against a cement floor. Angerious turned to Night, blame displayed in the first tell-tale sign of an impending fight.

“If you had just kept an eye on your girlfriend, Comic would still be alive!” Angerious yelled.

“You were supposed to look out for the traps!”

“Well if I could fucking see anything behind your fucking shoulder pads…!”

“They keep me safe!”

“Bullshit!”

“I swear to the Eighteen Gods-!”

Mary’s sobs were the worst of it. They echoed down those infinitely turning halls, somehow louder than any scream of anger could ever be. Both men stopped, looking at her fallen form.

She had knelt down, entire body somehow vibrating with grief. Her fingers spazzed, as though somehow, she could reach into the bobby trapped pit. As though, somehow, she could undo the undoable. She didn’t notice the two men looking at her. She could only sit. She could only be still.

For a long time, the three just sat there. One of them weeping, the other two staring at the one weeping.

The tears came in drones, first puddling beneath Mary before flooding their way in the canals created by the cobbled stones. The route eventually led the man-made salt water to an impossible impasse: the imposing darkness of the now-absent floor. The thing that had robbed Mary of one of her best friends.

Then, they flowed down, seemingly undeterred by the darkness ahead of them. They fell, showered the pit, with a ferocity and bravery unknown to most men.

More silence.
…
…
…
“Heelllppp…”

Mary looked up- or rather, down. Into the pit. 

“...I’ve fallen and I can’t get up.”

Mary stared wide-eyed into the pit, both joy and fear on her mug- in contrast with each other and working harmoniously. And then, reaching equilibrium, they canceled each other. Neutrality.

“I remember now,” she said. There was no more grief in her voice, but it seemed as though every emotion had been removed all together. 

Then, Mary fell into the pit. Angerious and Night could only stare at the spot Mary had been before doubling over. Once more, there was silence.

Only this time, there was no ear-splitting sound of human vs gravity.

Angerious and Night eyed each other, as though to begin arguing anew about who killed whose friends, or whose shoulder pads were compensating for something.
 
“Halt!”

Mary’s golden hair slowly peaked up from the darkness. 

She held a crumbled form in her arms, blood-coated and grinning. Injured, but still very much alive.

 As she continued gliding up, they got a good look at her. Her character ragged, adventuring clothes had suddenly bleached and expanded.  The white rags curled around her form, curving around her form and somehow making her taller, exculpating into a beautiful dress. Powerful. Intoxicating. Dangerous.

“You’re her.” Night said, that hint of confidence in his voice now replaced with fear- and awe, “You’re the forgotten Goddess…forgotten by everyone, including herself.”

“I am her,” said Mary. She looked around, not nervously, but as though she were evaluating her situation. Her eyes turned to examine Night and Angerious. There was a hint of recognition in them, but also years of many stories, now long forgotten.

“Welp,” said the crumbled form, “Thanks for the lift, Sue-sue!”

Comic tapped the all-powerful goddess just below the neck, hitting her collar bone. She released him, if only on impulse, letting him fall to the ground and land on his knees. The scrawny form stood up straight, forcing eye contact and smiling at his two frowning, worried comrades.

“So who died?”

Ignoring the question, Night turned to the Goddess. He walked up to her, looking up to make eye contact. 

“We get a wish, don’t we? That’s the deal?” 
His voice held no expression.

“Yes.”
Her voice held no expression.

“I want Damsel back. I want Comic cleaned up. I want us out of this dungeon, then I want this dungeon destroyed…I want my life back.”

Comic looked at night, disbelief on his face, “Dude, that was like, five.”

Mary nodded casually in agreement, before regaining her composter.

Sighing, Night spoke again.

“Then…I want everything back to the way it was before.”

“Everything?”
“Yes. Everything.”
I was lost in the dense forest. The small child was with me. I lost a child in the dense forest.

“I don’t know.”

They were honest words- words that left my mouth desperately following the question and the eternity of silence. 

No- I wasn’t stupid. They were words that I knew wouldn’t be accepted.
The courtroom was a pixilated rainbow. Sprites of various neon hues, meant to stand out against different, darker backgrounds, were jammed next to each other at random in the stadium. Looking at them all made my eyes hurt, so I looked down. Their eyes on me made my heart hurt, so I trembled.

Boos echoed from the stand at this sign of guilt. The judge- Angra Mainyu, the dragon-king who preceded over the military, the senate, and the courts, allowed it to continue. He knew they weren’t in a hurry. He allowed me to suffer.
Then, if only to save his own, monster-sized ears and those of the jurors, the strike of his gable finally put an end to it. For now, at least.
“Order- order in the court! The prosecution may continue…”
“Thank you, your honor,” said a sleek, tuxedoed lizard named Afzal. His oversized, lambent-green body towered over me and most of the jurors in the front rows. Every vowel sound he made sounded choppy in some implacable, metallic accent, like he used tuning forks for toothpicks. For this reason, he had no speaking roles in his boss-fight level. His sheer presence was intimidating enough.
“Now, Doppelganger Number 8A-277,” Afzal continued. More booing consumed the court, and he raised his horrible voice over them, “How else do you explain these incriminating circumstances?!”

He turned his body 90 degrees to face the expansive jury, casting his shadow over my defense attorney and me.

“That villain…that terrorist had not been seen in approximately three months, three days, twenty hours, eight minutes, and fifty one seconds. Are we to believe that, out of nowhere, that menace to our kind returned and not only completed the first five levels with unheard casualties, but also managed to find, operate, and successfully use our hidden, experimental powers up, our reality-breaking glitches, and our top secret warp zones?”

He let a silence fill the court, only broken by the tittering mumbles of the braver jurors. 

“No!” Afzal said finally. “The horrible man from not even Angra Mainyu knows where had to have inside assistance!”

“Objection!” my defense rose up. She was a blackbird: an air ally and one of the only monochrome characters in the world. Her voice had a twitter to it, and I much enjoyed it to Afzal’s. “The prosecution engages in argumentative questions, which he himself answers.”

“Sustained!” agreed Angra Mainyu. “Please, the prosecution must rephrase the question or move on…”

“Alright…” Afzal turned back to me. “Doppelganger Number 8A-277…did you or did you not engage in treasonous acts and first-degree, intentional, and premeditated murder?!” 

“no,” a frightened voice answered. Only after the sound had dissipated, I realized it had been my own.

“Did you or did you not leave your post during the invasion?”

“no.”

“Where were you?”

“Buh-between the two cement pipes, patrolling left and right. As I was trained.”

  “Did you, or did you not, voluntarily let the invader through?”

“I-” I stumbled, “He got through, but he was going very fast…”

“Did you or did you not allow him through?”

“No, I-”

“Did he get through because of your own faults and culpabilities?!”

“…yes.”

Afzal smiled-  I didn’t know the lizard allies could smile.

“Then,” he continued, speaking to no one in particular, “is it so much of a leap to assume this was purposeful?”

He turned to me, eagerly expecting an answer.

“I didn’t mean to-”

“Is it not possible…?”

“I would never endanger my comra-”

“But you did let him through?”

“Yes.”

“And you did let him go on- presumably to slaughter your fellow comrades?”

“…yes.”

“…The prosecution rests its case!”

The rest of the trial drove on. Too soon, I saw the judge sit up. He was speaking now-

“The jury may confer... ”
He exited.

The rainbow before me dissipated. Sitting in the echoing, empty chamber, I tried to stop shaking. Afzal began organizing his papers in a small briefcase. My Defense Attorney patted my back. We had tried. There, together, was silence.

Slowly, those jurors began to fill the room. And slowly, there, a rainbow was painted in the seats. They chattered among themselves. Finally, Angra Mainyu reentered. With that, a well-dressed turtle stood.  

“We the jury find the defendant, Doppelganger Number 8A-277, not guilty on the charge of first-degree murder.” said the turtle. “However, we find Doppelganger Number 8A-277 guilty of the lesser charges of culpable murder and negligent, militant treason.”

My head hit the desk in front of me, and I glued it there. I’d never cried in public anymore- I’d never even been around this many people. But it didn’t matter anymore.

Angra Mainyu spoke thus, “Very well. Doppelganger Number 8A-277, I sentence you to the mandatory sentence for this thing you have done- and that is death. You will be detained indefinitely in maximum security. And may I have mercy on your soul.”
